A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MagEdgePool and SpreadEdgePool research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the expanded later version.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph classification, feature reconstruction, structure preservation, and runtime results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds molecular regression, additional baseline comparisons, randomized controls, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The exact pooling procedure remains substantially unchanged. Appendix D.2.2 adds concrete MagEdgePool* and SpreadEdgePool* variants that update distances using minimum distances to original nodes; v1 only suggested distance updating as a possible approximation. Algorithm 1 also revises the bookkeeping for excluding adjacent edges.

E1.justification: v2 retains the existing classification and reconstruction coverage and adds molecular property regression on MolEsol, MolFreesolv, and MolLipo (Section 4.4 and Appendix C.2). This introduces a distinct prediction task beyond v1's evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: EdgePool, discussed but not experimentally compared in v1, becomes an evaluated classification and efficiency baseline in v2. Table S.9 also introduces a randomized pooling comparator. These additions address substantial gaps in comparisons with learned edge contraction and unguided pooling.

E3.justification: The main classification protocol is retained. New regression experiments use predefined OGB splits, MSE training, RMSE evaluation, a linear readout, two-convolution blocks, and early-stopping patience of 100. Additional experiments introduce fixed 200-epoch GIN cost measurements, graph-size scaling tests, and a PyTorch implementation for the EdgePool comparison.

E4.justification: v2 adds a randomized pooling ablation testing the value of geometry guidance, exact-versus-approximate computational comparisons, and runtime/memory scaling analyses. It also extends structure-preservation analysis to ENZYMES, DHFR, and PROTEINS. The earlier reconstruction, correlation, and pooling-ratio analyses remain.

E5.justification: Existing standard-deviation reporting and Wilcoxon tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction remain. Appendix D.5 adds Friedman and Nemenyi tests across dataset-level mean scores. New experiments disclose ten seeded regression repeats and five scaling repeats; these do not establish increased runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: The shared classification and reconstruction tables retain identical numerical entries. v2 adds regression RMSEs, EdgePool and randomized-control accuracies, computational measurements, and additional structure-preservation results. Newly reported aggregate rankings are not fully consistent with the retained table: Figure S.5 gives NDP rank 4.2, while Table 1 still reports 3.6.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds formal expressivity analysis, including Select-Reduce-Connect definitions, cited sufficient conditions in Theorem 7, and a new Corollary 3 with proof for sum aggregation. v2 also revises the operator/eigenvalue description in Section 2.3 and statements of Theorems 2–3. Most earlier magnitude/spread proofs remain.

C1.justification: The central claims about diversity-guided edge pooling, structural preservation, and stable classification performance remain. The conclusion extends the claim of competitive task performance to graph regression, which was not established or claimed in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: v1 already acknowledged redundancy, homophily, and tasks where structure preservation may be unnecessary. v2 develops dataset-specific interpretations of randomized pooling, discusses the costs and benefits of learned edge scores, and explicitly recommends small-to-medium sparse graphs. These substantially clarify mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v1 referred readers to a supplementary code submission. v2 supplies GitHub access information for a BSD-licensed PyTorch implementation, identifies additional experimental software, and documents approximation rules, regression configurations, and separate preprocessing/training measurements. These materially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through a global-versus-hierarchical pooling discussion, including SOPool and DKEPool, references on diffusion approximations, and detailed engagement with prior randomized-pooling findings in Appendix D.7. The original claim of introducing magnitude to graph learning remains.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the principal narrative remain recognizable, with copyediting and expanded explanations. v2 adds roadmaps, an appendix contents page and conference checklist, subdivides the efficiency discussion, and moves the overview-experiment setup from D.4 to C.5.1.

P2.justification: v2 adds regression and computational tables, the EdgePool/randomized-control table, scaling plots, critical-difference diagrams, and additional structure-preservation panels. Existing displays are largely retained and relocated or renumbered; the correlation panels in v1 Figure 5 are rearranged into v2 Figure S.1.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves important empirical gaps by evaluating EdgePool and randomized pooling and by exposing preprocessing costs separately from training costs. These additions substantially improve assessment of whether geometry guidance is useful and computationally practical; explicit code access further improves reproducibility. Remaining qualifications include unreconciled rankings between Table 1 and Figure S.5, dependence of total-cost comparisons on preprocessing reuse, and an expressivity proof restricted to sum aggregation while the default algorithm averages features.
